newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Renault's Brazil unit posts 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Renault's Brazil unit posts 1996 loss.

text.p: French carmaker Renault's Brazilian sales unit said it posted a loss of 30.9 million reais ($29.1 million) last year due to heavy marketing investments to introduce its brand in the country.

Ana Thereza Kastrup, spokeswoman at Renault's local sales unit Renault Comercial do Brasil, said 1996 "was the year of Renault's installation in Brazil" so no comparative figures for the previous year were available.
Renault plans to invest $1 billion in Brazil by 2002 to build a car plant and establish a network of Renault auto distributors, Kastrup said.
Last year, the firm "invested heavily in infrastructure," she said.

Renault Automoveis do Brasil, which owns Renault Comercial, is building a car plant in the southeastern state of Parana. The plant is expected to start producing Renault's mid-sized Megane cars in November 1998.
Kastrup said Renault Comercial, which has 22 distributors, posted net revenues of 103.3 million reais last year.
In 1997's first quarter, the company sold 2,276 cars in Brazil, up 84.3 percent from 1,235 cars sold in the same period last year. Sales this year are expected double to 16,000 cars.
